📢 The internet isn’t just for humans anymore, it’s being rewritten for AI

Imagine opening a website and discovering that some of the “ads” weren’t meant for you at all.

That’s exactly what Time is experimenting with.

The publication has introduced a new type of advertisement designed specifically for AI assistants like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. Instead of flashy banners or videos, these ads are simple, fact-filled text that AI models can use when answering users’ questions about brands.

It’s a sign of how quickly the web is changing.

For years, companies fought to rank #1 on Google. Now they’re chasing something entirely different: making sure AI mentions their brand when someone asks for a recommendation or explanation.

😐 Grok 4.6 Launch Set for Next Week

Elon Musk announced that Grok 4.6 will launch on August 7 with 1.5T parameters. Grok 4.7 is planned to follow just weeks later.

Around the same time, rumors surfaced about Composer 3, developed by Cursor under SpaceX. It was trained from scratch on the Colossus 2 cluster and aims to match Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol quality at a fraction of the cost.

💻 Radeon RX 9050 Returns with 4GB VRAM

ASRock listed the Radeon RX 9050 with 4GB of video memory, the first modern card with this capacity in years. It features RDNA 4 architecture, 16 compute units, and a boost clock up to 2600 MHz, but only a 64-bit memory bus and 18 GB/s bandwidth.

The 4GB VRAM is well below current AAA game recommendations, limiting play to 1080p with no future-proofing. The card appeared in a Best Buy prebuilt priced at $889, paired with 8GB DDR4 RAM, a 500GB SSD, and a Ryzen 5 5500 CPU.

Higher memory costs and component shortages force manufacturers to cut specs rather than raise prices. The 4GB card is a sign of how tight the market remains, making this low VRAM configuration acceptable again.

📱 Honor Robot Phone Unboxed Early

A Weibo video shows the Honor Robot Phone before launch. Its robotic arm unfolds in 0.8 seconds when the lens cover slides open, with an on-screen animation, and folds flush when idle.

Honor’s phone features 360-degree stabilization via a three-axis optical system, a four-degree mechanical gimbal, a coprocessor, and AI, reaching a CIPA rating of 5.5. It has a 200MP main sensor on the gimbal, a 50MP ultrawide, and a 200MP periscope lens, color-tuned with ARRI cinema cameras.

Preorders in China need a 1000 yuan deposit and include lifetime YOYO AI SVIP, a year of free gimbal replacement, accessories, 24-month installments, and trade-in options. The price is undisclosed. The official reveal is in August.

Boris Cherny, the creator behind Claude Code, has launched his longest-running prompt to date.

This automated run has been active for 15 consecutive days. Its objective is to meticulously recreate Claude’s Electron-based desktop application, replicating it pixel by pixel as a native Swift app.
